rules.title: Rules reference
rules.subtitle: Part C — Lights and Shapes (Rules 20–31), plus the Rule 3 definitions they depend on. Paragraph-keyed and deep-linkable.
rules.corpusNote: Rule text is quoted verbatim from the package corpus you pick below and is never translated by this app. Every paragraph shows its corpus's tier and source (REQ-LANG-3). A paragraph the chosen corpus lacks says so and shows the fallback (REQ-LANG-7); a rule where some paragraphs fell back is labelled a mixed rendering.
rules.knownOmissions.title: Recorded omissions in the applicability data
rules.knownOmissions.intro: colregs records five places where its settled applicability table deliberately stops short of the rule text. They are data (known_omissions), not silence — surfaced here so the gap is visible.
rules.amendment.title: Which consolidation is this? Citations move.
rules.amendment.p1: The paragraph paths here belong to the {instrument}, edition {edition}: amended through {amended}, in force {inForce} (colregs editions.json, REQ-LANG-10). The {corpus} corpus declares that as the edition its text reflects — {status}.
rules.amendment.p2: A citation's meaning has moved before. Seven IMO amendment resolutions have touched the Rules since 1972, and two of them renumbered Part C: A.910(22) (2001, in force 2003) added the WIG-craft paragraph as 23(c) "and renumber accordingly" — the small-vessel alternative that had been 23(c) since 1972 was displaced to 23(d). A.464(XII) (1981) relettered 24(g) to 24(h). A study note citing "Rule 23(c)" means a different light in a 1995 textbook than it does today.

sound.title: Sound signals — Part D (Rules 32–37)
sound.provisional: Sound is the third panel of an encounter: manoeuvring signals (Rule 34) are what a vessel sounds when she acts, and restricted-visibility signals (Rule 35) are what you hear before you see anything. The patterns and the audio here are searoom's own, provisional: colregs carries no Part D data yet, because the question of how to model event-triggered signals (Q-1) is still open upstream. The rule text slot below each signal stays empty until it does.
sound.noAudio: This browser has no Web Audio; the patterns are shown but cannot be sounded.
sound.jurisdictionNote: These signals are the international ones. {jurisdiction} is not modelled for Part D — Inland manoeuvring signals in particular are signals of intent, not of action.
sound.rule.35: Rule 35 — sound signals in restricted visibility
sound.attention: No pattern to play: Rule 36 allows any light or sound signal that cannot be mistaken for one of the signals above. That is the content of the paragraph, not a gap in the data.
sound.timing: {glyphs} — {seconds} s in all, at Rule 32 durations (a short blast about one second, a prolonged one four to six).
sound.repeat: Repeated at intervals of not more than {seconds} seconds.
sound.textPending: The text of Rule {paragraph} is not in the corpus. colregs' rule-text corpora stop at Rule 31, and REQ-PART-3 requires the Q-1 ADR before any Part D data is written — so searoom shows you the signal and names the paragraph, and will not transcribe the rule itself.

drawer.title: Data drawer
blocker.q11: inherit-by-absence is verified unsafe (silence at Rule 28 would assert international law on inland waters); no non-intl jurisdiction lands until an explicit suppression mechanism (tombstones) exists.
blocker.q3.ca: the Reproduction of Federal Law Order is recalled, not verified; REQ-PROV-2 blocks the jurisdiction until its terms are checked against the primary source.
blocker.q3.cevni: CEVNI's UN copyright is unclear, and colregs names it the licence check most likely to fail outright.
blocker.q3.de: §5 UrhG (amtliche Werke) is the presumed basis and is unverified.
blocker.q3.uk: OGL v3.0 is the recalled basis and is unverified.
blocker.q3.au: CC BY 4.0 is the recalled basis and is unverified.
blocker.q7: the source's reproduction terms are unchecked; licence, not translation effort, sequences every corpus.
blocker.q1: do sound signals fit the entry model at all, or do they need an event dimension? REQ-PART-3 requires an ADR before any Part D data is written.
blocker.part2: day shapes use the same entry model, differing only in the vocabulary they emit.
blocker.part4: Part B governs conduct between two vessels; the fact record is single-vessel by construction.
blocker.lang8: a community corpus needs a named human producer and reviewer; machine translation without named review is not accepted.
sp.jurisdictions.title: Jurisdictions
sp.jurisdictions.intro: Jurisdiction is a dimension of the data, not a fork of the app (colregs REQ-SCOPE-2). International is live; the rest are signposted with what colregs has actually measured and what blocks each, by name.
sp.parts.title: Rule parts
sp.corpora.title: Rule-text corpora
sp.intl.label: International (COLREGS 72)
sp.intl.p1: Live: 40 applicability entries, 100 rule-text paragraphs, 10 light definitions, 53 fixture cases — Part C (Rules 20–31), night only.
sp.intl.p2: Five omissions are recorded in the data itself (known_omissions): 24(d)'s second-masthead requirement for towing vessels; the 24(f)–(i) pushed/towed-group family; 27(c)'s severely-restricted tow; 27(g)'s under-12 m exemption; and Rule 31 seaplanes/WIG. Searoom shows them as first-class gaps in the Rules reference, not silence.
sp.us-inland.label: US Inland (33 CFR 83–90)
sp.us-inland.p1: Delta measured 2026-08-30, paragraph-by-paragraph against eCFR: of 90 Part C paths, 15 are same-path-different-text — the dangerous case, where the citation you'd copy across means something else: 22(a)/(b)/(c), 24(c)/(d)/(f)/(g)/(i), 25(d)(i)/(ii), 25(e), 26(d), 27(c), 30(e).
sp.us-inland.p2: One structural path mismatch: 23(d)(i) has no Inland counterpart path — the content sits at bare 83.23(d). One whole-rule clean absence: Rule 28 is "[Reserved]" — constrained-by-draught is not an Inland concept at all. Two clean intl-only absences (23(d)(ii)/(iii)). Roughly 71 of 90 paths are citation-compatible.
sp.us-inland.p3: One new light: 83.21(g), the special flashing light — yellow, 50–70 flashes per minute, forward, showing over an arc of 180–225° — which propagates into the 22(a)/(b)/(c) range table and 24(f).
sp.us-inland.p4: Six Inland-only insertion blocks: 23(e) Great Lakes substitution, 24(j) Western Rivers pushing/towing, 26(f) fishing-proximity signals lifted inline from Annex II, 27(d)(iv) dredge pipelines, and the large 30(g)–(l) anchorage block.
sp.us-inland.geo: Great Lakes, Western Rivers and special anchorage areas sit under US Inland as geography facts a predicate reads, not as jurisdictions of their own (REQ-SCOPE-5) — their CFR paths are 83.23(e), 83.24(j) and 83.30(g)–(l).
sp.ca-inland.label: Canada (Collision Regulations, C.R.C. c.1416)
sp.ca-inland.p1: Ranked moderate on colregs' jurisdiction queue (ADR 0001); no paragraph-level diff has been run.
sp.eu-cevni.label: EU inland waterways (UNECE CEVNI / RPNR)
sp.eu-cevni.p1: The largest delta of any jurisdiction on the queue: genuinely different inland light configurations, and no prior art as structured data anywhere.
sp.eu-cevni.p2: This is the only candidate where the licence check could end the jurisdiction rather than delay it. Signposted honestly: highest value, highest risk of never existing.
sp.de-binnen.label: Germany (SeeSchStrO / BinSchStrO)
sp.de-binnen.p1: Ranked large on colregs' jurisdiction queue (ADR 0001); not measured.
sp.uk.label: UK (SI 1996/75)
sp.au.label: Australia (Marine Order 30)
sp.uk-au.p1: Near-zero delta, and on the queue precisely because of that: it costs almost nothing and lets the coverage statement name six jurisdictions honestly. A near-zero delta is itself a teaching point about what the 1972 harmonisation achieved.
sp.day-shapes.label: Day shapes
sp.day-shapes.p1: Night is live; day is signposted. Shapes use the same entry model as lights and differ only in the vocabulary they emit (REQ-PART-2) — this is modelled-for and unwritten, not unresolved.
sp.part-d.label: Part D — sound and light signals (Rules 32–37)
sp.part-d.p1: Not "coming soon": undecided, and here is the decision. colregs Q-1 asks whether Part D fits the entry model at all — signals are event-triggered (a manoeuvre, a bend, restricted visibility) where lights are state-derived from a fact record.
sp.part-d.p2: REQ-PART-3 requires that divergence to be recorded as an ADR before any Part D data is written. When that ADR lands upstream, this mode lights up by bumping a dependency.
sp.part-b.label: Part B — steering and sailing rules
sp.part-b.p1: Deliberately out of scope, and may never be modelled (REQ-PART-4): Part B governs conduct between two vessels, and colregs' fact record describes one vessel by construction. A dead end that is a dead end on purpose — it explains the shape of everything else here.
sp.locale.fact1: Licence, not translation effort, is what sequences this work (colregs Q-7): each corpus is blocked on establishing a lawful, reproducible source, not on finding translators. And Q-7 is answerable per language — clearing one source unblocks that corpus alone.
sp.locale.fact2: The first non-English corpus was a design gate upstream (colregs GATE-2), not just a file: it forced the instrument → edition → corpus layering decision. ADR 0013 took it — corpora are files under a declared edition — and the Spanish and Finnish corpora are the first to land under it.
sp.en-us.label: English — USCG amalgamated
sp.en-us.p1: Live, and the reference corpus every other one falls back to. It is the USCG amalgamated rendition — national tier, en-US — not the authentic treaty English: Article IX of the Convention makes English and French the equally authentic texts, and this one reads "maneuver" where the treaty reads "manoeuvre".
sp.en-us.p2: Its four transcription defects against its own declared source — 21(a), 21(b), 23(b), 29(b) — were tracked as colregs #6, now closed. The teaching point stands: even the English text you study from is one national rendition of a multilingual instrument.
sp.fi.label: Suomi — Finlex
sp.fi.p1: Live: Finlex, SopS 30/1977, national tier. Licence verified 2026-09-12 — Tekijänoikeuslaki 404/1961 §9 puts treaties and their official translations outside copyright, and Finlex publishes as open data (CC BY 4.0).
sp.fi.p2: The transcription is tracked in colregs #98. Until it is complete, a paragraph missing from the Finnish corpus says so and shows the en-US text, labelled — never silently. The Finnish display language is a separate choice above and remains a draft awaiting native review (REQ-LANG-8).
sp.fr.label: Français — UNTS
sp.fr.p1: Authentic tier: Article IX, verified 2026-08-30 against the UNTS deposit, makes French equally authentic with English. Blocked: the deposit's reproduction terms were checked (colregs #81) and do not permit redistribution.
sp.en-unts.label: English — UNTS original
sp.en-unts.p1: The authentic treaty English. Blocked on the same UNTS reproduction terms as the French text (colregs #81); the USCG rendition stays the English corpus.
sp.es.label: Español — BOE
sp.ru.label: Русский
sp.zh.label: 中文
sp.zh.p1: Official tier: the mechanism is verified (IMO's six official languages) and a Chinese edition is catalogued. Catalogued means for sale — the lawful reproducible source is still the open half.
sp.ar.label: العربية
sp.ar.p1: Official tier — and the one sub-claim colregs flags as not confirmed to the same standard as the rest: the Arabic edition's product page returned 403 to the verification pass, so its availability rests on search-result paraphrase. A verification gap besides the licence question.
sp.de.label: Deutsch
sp.de.p1: Named in ADR 0003 as a state gazetting a binding translation; no source or terms have been identified. Not yet scoped.
sp.community.label: Community translations
sp.community.p1: No community corpus exists and none is named. The bar is REQ-LANG-8: a named human producer and a named reviewer are mandatory — machine translation without named review is not accepted.

rules.differs.link: colregs ADR 0020 — the skeleton is a delta
corpus.switcher.title: Rule-text corpus
corpus.switcher.note: Switching corpus changes the words and nothing else. Entry ids, paragraph paths, the lights and the quiz answers are language-neutral (REQ-LANG-2). Tier is the source's legal authority, never the language's (REQ-LANG-3).
corpus.paragraphCount: {count, plural, =0 {no paragraphs transcribed yet} one {# paragraph} other {# paragraphs}} of {total}
fallback.withheld: {wanted} models this paragraph but withholds its text: {reason}.
blocker.q7.unts: the UNTS deposit's reproduction terms were checked (colregs #81) and are confirmed blocking: the treaty deposit is not ours to redistribute.
blocker.issue98: colregs #98 — the Finnish transcription is in progress; every paragraph not yet transcribed says so and shows the en-US text.
sp.es.p1: Live: the Spanish instrument of accession as published by the Agencia Estatal Boletín Oficial del Estado. Licence verified 2026-09-09 under the BOE aviso legal — reuse permitted, commercial and non-commercial, with attribution; a consolidated text must not be represented as official.
sp.es.p2: Tier and source are shown beside every paragraph. Paragraphs not yet transcribed fall back to the en-US text and say so.
sp.ru.p1: Official tier: a deposited official translation, verified against Article IX. The source is the problem, not the text — IMO's consolidated editions are sold publications and probably not reproducible; a national gazette is the likely lawful route.
fallback.all: Nothing in this set comes from the corpus you picked: all {total} paragraphs are shown from {shown}. This is the fallback corpus's rendering, not a mixed one.
